base_member_text: [L413-L494] (MED/message-size contract) Sendrecv wrappers use size(sendbuf) for both send and receive counts without validating recvbuf's extent.
audit_member_text: [L413-L496] (MED/buffer-size-contract) Every sendrecv overload derives both the send and receive MPI counts solely from size(sendbuf) and never checks recvbuf size, so a mismatched caller can overrun or incompletely fill the receive object.

base_member_text: [L374-L406] (MED/string buffer bounds) Character broadcast does not check that each receiver's character variable is at least as long as the source string before assigning x(i:i).
audit_member_text: [L387-L407] (MED/bounds-contract) Character broadcast sends the root's trimmed length but never verifies that receiving character variables are at least that long before assigning x(i:i), so differing declared lengths can write out of bounds.

base_member_text: [L245-L280,L737-L855] (MED/domain-size precondition) Processor-grid construction has no minimum local-domain check even though halo shifts subsequently index fixed positions up to four cells from each boundary.
audit_member_text: [L737-L856] (MED/bounds-contract) The ranged shift routines accept arbitrary i1/i2 and derive sections using a fixed four-cell overlap without validating ordering or array extents; the rank-3 version is additionally marked in-source as not correct.

base_member_text: [L954-L1005] (MED/unchecked row contract) xmpi_getrow uses n and prow directly without checking the source row length, destination extent, or processor-row range.
audit_member_text: [L954-L1005] (MED/mpi/input-contract) xmpi_getrow does not validate prow, n, size(a,2), or size(b), so invalid metadata can yield an invalid source rank, shape-nonconforming assignment, buffer mismatch, or a blocking receive that never matches.

base_member_text: [L151-L177,L297-L570,L948,L995-L1005] (LOW/unchecked MPI status) MPI return codes are stored throughout but never inspected and no communicator error handler is installed in this implementation.
audit_member_text: [L151-L177,L185,L297-L371,L424-L570,L948,L995-L1005] (MED/mpi/error-handling) MPI return codes are repeatedly written to local variables and never checked, so failed collectives or point-to-point operations can silently leave state invalid or ranks divergent.

base_member_text: [L62-L73] (HIGH/serial API mismatch) The non-MPI branch defines xmpirank and xmpisize instead of the subsystem's xmpi_rank and xmpi_size names and omits xomaster, xcompute, and xmpi_orank, making this module incompatible with serial consumers of the current API.

[L75-L86,L139;L189-L193;L945-L949] (HIGH/MPI API drift) This alternative module provides only one-argument broadcasts, a processor-grid routine without cyclic input, and a zero-argument barrier, while the surrounding subsystem calls the corresponding multi-communicator/cyclic forms.
[L101-L107,L674-L693] (HIGH/missing generic implementation) xmpi_shift_i3 passes rank-3 integer sections to xmpi_sendrecv, but that generic has no rank-3 integer procedure.

audit_member_text: [L143-L178] (MED/mpi/lifecycle) The wrapper unconditionally calls MPI_Init and MPI_Finalize without checking MPI_Initialized or MPI_Finalized, which makes it unsafe to embed in a host that owns the MPI lifecycle.

[L201-L220] (LOW/integer-range) Automatic processor-grid selection computes border lengths in default integers and uses a hard-coded 1000000000 sentinel, so sufficiently large grid dimensions can overflow or fail to select a factorization.

[L360-L365] (LOW/mpi/portability) The integer*8 broadcast relies on the nonstandard MPI_INTEGER8 datatype name and nonstandard kind syntax rather than matching a selected Fortran kind to an MPI datatype.

[L586-L703] (MED/bounds-contract) The basic shift routines index fixed interior rows or columns such as 2, m-1, and n-1 without enforcing minimum extents, so small local partitions can access outside their arrays.
